title: Re-key directive registry by gap code and delete appliesTo matcher
description: WHY: registry entries currently predict enforcement with appliesTo predicates (packages/core/src/agent-directive-registry.ts lines 57-61 for example blocked.resolve-blockers firing on workStatuses blocked), duplicating what deriveReadinessStatus and applyRequiredCloseoutGatePolicy already know. WHAT: restructure each registry entry to be keyed by one or more EnforcementGap codes from sprint 2; the entry carries instruction text, a mandatory nextCommand template (a directive that cannot name its command is documentation, not a directive - flag any entry that cannot and raise with the owner rather than inventing), audience, and a typed data slot contract matching the gap payload. Delete the appliesTo predicate model. Migrate the existing families (blocked, verification, review, audit, git, closeout, doctor, memory, handoff, container, phase, sprint, workflow_next) by mapping each to its gap codes; workflow_next and memory families have no enforcement gap - key those off explicit advisory gap codes emitted by their commands rather than keeping a second matching path. Keep the registry a checked-in constant with the same version discipline (AGENT_DIRECTIVE_REGISTRY_VERSION) and preserve the instruction-text safety boundary from docs/architecture/AGENT_DIRECTIVES.md verbatim.
acceptanceCriteria: Every registry entry is keyed by gap code with zero appliesTo predicates remaining
Every entry has a nextCommand or a recorded owner decision for the exceptions
Registry unit tests validate one-to-one coverage between the gap-code enumeration and registry keys, with intentional no-directive gaps listed explicitly
closedReason: Completed registry inversion with checkpoint 2ed725e0c652ed90caddcb2d2924149ad31c953a; verification and review gates satisfied; summary bw_summary_7324b1d38aeec07a recorded.
